prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single transparent-background pixel-art tree sprite for a 2D dungeon-adventure tileset.
The attached image is the EDIT TARGET, a tiny 16x28 green tree. Remaster this SAME tree at fourfold logical pixel resolution, final target 64 pixels wide by 112 pixels high, portrait aspect 4:7. Render the pixel sprite enlarged with crisp square logical pixels, so meaningful one-pixel details remain readable after reduction to 64x112.
Keep the original distinctive narrow, pointed teardrop / compact conifer silhouette, upright orientation, the very short brown trunk at bottom center, the cool teal-green / emerald foliage palette and subtle upper-left lighting. Keep original proportions and approximately the same footprint; a single centered complete tree occupies nearly the entire portrait canvas with only a very thin transparent margin. This is a front-facing game map tree sprite, not an overhead circular tree and not an isometric environment.
Add carefully hand-pixeled foliage detail: small irregular overlapping needle/leaf clusters, several readable tiered foliage layers, restrained mint-green highlights on upper-left cluster tips, rich dark green crevices, lower and right-side foliage shadow, a few subtle brown bark pixels on the tiny trunk. Richer craftsmanship than the source, but coherent large forms, limited color palette and clean stair-step silhouette. Fine surface texture should complement the recent detailed pixel dungeon wall and floor assets.
True transparent alpha background. No sky, backdrop, ground plane, grass at the base, rocks, snow, ornaments, flowers, fruit, extra trees, cast shadow, text, grid or watermark. No photographic foliage, painterly brushwork, blur, smooth gradients, 3D rendering, vector art or antialiasing. Keep the entire pointed crown and trunk inside the canvas, don't crop any tree pixels.
